THIS CRIMINAL MISC. CASE HAVING COME UP FOR ADMISSION ON 27.11.2025, ALONG WITH Crl.MC.4297/2020, THE COURT ON THE SAME DAY PASSED THE FOLLOWING:
 2025:KER:91606 Crl.M.C.No.4297 & 2890 of 2020  4  ORDER The petitioner in Crl.M.C.No.2890/2020 is the first accused and the petitioners in Crl.M.C.No.4297/2020 are the accused Nos 2 to 4 in C.C.No.220/2020 on the files of the Judicial First Class Magistrate Court-I, Kothamangalam, which arose out of Crime No.428/2020 of the Kothamangalam Police Station, in connection with the allegation of commission of offences under Sections 153 and 271 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860, Sections 118(e) and 120 (o) of the Kerala Police Act, 2011 and Section 4(2)(i) read with Section 5 of the Kerala Epidemic Diseases Ordinance, 2020.

2. The prosecution case is that on 30.03.2020, the petitioners made propaganda through Facebook, making use of the cell phone of the first petitioner, that the community kitchen being maintained by Nellikuzhi Grama Panchayath under the presidentship of the defacto complainant,
has been serving sub standard food, and collecting huge amount from the public for the same.
According to the prosecution, the aforesaid propaganda made during COVID period, was intended to give provocation to cause riot.
3. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioners and the learned Public Prosecutor representing the State of Kerala.

The allegation against the petitioners is that they made publication through Facebook, criticising the food being distributed through the community kitchen of Nellikuzhi Grama Panchayat, by making the following posts.

sentences.text: It is true that the propaganda made in the above regard, at a time when our State was reeling under the menace of COVID epidemic, was a thing, which should be deprecated.
Such a publication causing insecurity feeling in the minds of the people, who were under the terror of the spread of epidemic, cannot be said to be one made with good intention.

But at the same time, it is pertinent to note that the propaganda allegedly made by the petitioners in the above regard, cannot be said to be of such a gravity, as to constitute the offence under Section 153 IPC.

It is not possible to say that the propaganda made in the above regard would cause the offence of rioting, as envisaged under Section 153 IPC.
6.

Likewise, it is not possible to say that the aforesaid act alleged against the petitioners are capable of bringing home the offence under Section 271 IPC, which relates to the quarantine applicable to vessels.

For charging a person with the commission of offence under Section 118(e) of the Kerala Police Act, 2011, there should be sufficient materials to show that such person knowingly did any act,
which caused danger to the public,or failure in public safety.
In the given set of facts of the case, it is not possible to say that the allegations levelled against the petitioners are capable of attracting the aforesaid offence as well.
8. Section 120 of the Kerala Police Act, deals with the penalty for causing nuisance and violation of public order.

The offence under Section 120(o) of the Kerala Police Act will be attracted, if it is shown that a person, by way of any means of communication, caused nuisance of himself to any other person by repeated or undesirable or anonymous call, letter, writing, message, e-mail or through a messenger.
9. The case on hand does not come within the purview of the aforesaid offence envisaged under Section 120(o) of the Kerala Police Act.

10. For proceeding against a person in connection with the penal provisions contained in Section 5 of the Kerala Epidemic Diseases Ordinance, 2020 (which later on became the Kerala Epidemic Diseases Act, 2021), it has to be shown that a person who is bound by regulations or order thereunder, contravened or disobeyed such regulations or order, or obstructed any officer empowered under that ordinance.
As far as the present case is concerned, nothing of that sort are brought out from the prosecution records.

Hence, 2025:KER:91606 Crl.M.C.No.4297 & 2890 of 2020 the offences under Section 4(2)(i) and 5 of the Kerala Epidemic Diseases Ordinance, 2020, are also not attracted in the facts and circumstances of the case.
